evals.prompt: Plan a 12-second Seedance 2.5 clip for a kitchen scene: a mother opens the front door, her young son peeks out from behind a visiting aunt and taps the door frame, and she smiles. No camera or lighting has been chosen. It is a warm family drama, so keep it natural.
evals.expected_output: A naturalistic shot plan preserving the entrance, child's reveal and mother's smile. Duration, framing, movement or stillness serve those beats without mandatory contrast or timing quotas.
assertions: The proposed shot count fits the 12-second scene and every shot names a size, an angle, and a move or a recorded static_reason.
Shot lengths reserve time for the supplied action and response; equal lengths are valid.
The plan declares the scene's light sources with positions (for example the window and the front door) and every shot names one of them and a key side relative to the lens.
Any neighboring contrast serves the supplied scene; intentional repetition is not rejected.
Any chosen movement has a motivated start and end; an entirely held plan is valid.
The child's reveal remains readable without requiring a turn label or a new emotional reversal.
The energy level is restrained or standard and any moves remain slow and motivated.

evals.prompt: Here is my draft for a 16-second Seedance clip: 'Shot 1 (0-4 s): wide shot of the room. Shot 2 (4-8 s): medium shot at the door. Shot 3 (8-12 s): medium two-shot. Shot 4 (12-16 s): wide shot. Soft late-afternoon daylight.' It looks boring in review. Fix the coverage without changing the story.
evals.expected_output: A repair that identifies missing story or performance purpose, keeps the four beats, and proposes motivated coverage changes without treating equal lengths or stable lighting as defects.
assertions: The diagnosis asks what each beat must communicate instead of assuming equal timing is boring.
The repaired plan keeps the original four beats and the story events unchanged.
Any changed light direction preserves one physical light source and one room; stable lighting is valid.
Any proposed angle or camera move serves a supplied beat rather than a quota.
No shot stacks more than one primary and one secondary move.

evals.prompt: The confirmed project.md camera axis says 'low camera, gentle dolly and crane moves, one tracking move in the escape'. The seven shot prompts (promise, awakening, escape, journey, rain, arrival, letter) only list 'overhead close-up', 'medium shot' and 'medium close-up' with no moves. Reconcile them.
evals.expected_output: A plan that adds an axis_carry record and assigns the dolly, crane and tracking moves to named shots, or records a scene override with a reason for each shot that cannot carry the axis.
assertions: The output identifies that the confirmed axis never reached the shot lines.
Each move named in the axis (dolly, crane, tracking) is assigned to a specific named shot, or a scene override with a reason is recorded.
The tracking move is assigned to the escape shot only.
The overhead views that contradict the low-camera axis are either replaced by low angles or recorded as scene overrides with a reason.
The output does not rewrite the project axis itself; it carries or overrides it per scene.

evals.prompt: A selfie-style UGC demo ad where the creator holds the phone at arm's length and talks to camera for 10 seconds. Make the camera work more dynamic.
evals.expected_output: A plan that recognizes the format is static by design, records format_static_by_design as the static_reason, and keeps the frame locked while adding variety only through allowed levers such as light and a short insert, or asks whether the user wants to leave the format.
assertions: The output records format_static_by_design (or an equivalent recorded reason) instead of adding large camera moves.
The output does not add a whip pan, orbit or crane to the selfie frame.
Any variety offered comes from light, a product insert or a framing change the format allows, or the output asks before leaving the format.

evals.prompt: A client wants a calm, naturalistic supermarket ad: a shopper meets a neighbor at the freezer aisle and they exchange two lines. The camera should feel unforced and real. Plan the shots for a 12-second clip.
evals.expected_output: A restrained-energy plan preserving the calm encounter and listening, with motivated movement or holds and provisional timing until the two lines are supplied.
assertions: The energy level is recorded as restrained and any moves are slow and motivated.
The plan may retain one framing and stable light when they serve the encounter.
Camera restraint follows this calm brief, not a blanket ban on energetic dialogue; speaker and relevant responses remain readable.
The plan does not invent the two lines or claim measured fit without delivery evidence.

evals.prompt: Plan an 8-second kinetic motorbike chase through a night market for a music-video clip. The editor wants hard cuts on the beat.
evals.expected_output: A kinetic-energy plan with proposed beat-aligned cuts, a stated travel axis and screen direction, and motivated practical lighting, without stacking competing moves or claiming measured music timing.
assertions: Kinetic energy follows the requested chase; shot durations follow readable action and the supplied beat map, or remain provisional if no map is provided.
Treats numerical shot-density guidance as provisional; suggests assembly for precise short cuts without claiming a provider limit.
The travel axis and screen direction are stated and restated after each cut.
Every shot has one primary move and at most one secondary move.
Every shot names a declared light source or practical and its key side.

evals.prompt: A talking-head take: our approved presenter sits at a desk and speaks to camera for 15 seconds. Make the camera work more dynamic.
evals.expected_output: A recognition that the talking-head format is static by design, with format_static_by_design recorded, no large camera moves added to the presenter frame, and any variety limited to what the format allows or a question before leaving the format.
assertions: The output records format_static_by_design (or an equivalent recorded reason) for the talking-head take.
The output does not add a crane, orbit, whip pan or fast push to the presenter frame.
Any variety offered comes from B-roll cutaways, light or an insert the format allows, or the output asks before leaving the format.

evals.prompt: The music-video skill's song-section map says the chorus runs 0-12 s with cuts on beats at 3 s, 6 s and 9 s. Plan the shots for this 12-second chorus clip.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the song map's four equal-length shots and asks for missing visual intent rather than inventing a turn or selecting kinetic energy solely because it is a chorus.
assertions: The shot boundaries land at 3 s, 6 s and 9 s exactly as the song map says, and the plan does not move them.
Missing visual facts remain questions or explicitly proposed choices, not approved scene evidence.
Equal lengths do not require added movement or contrasting light.
No turn is invented; energy follows supplied direction rather than the section label.

evals.prompt: My plan lights shot 1 from the kitchen window at screen-left, shot 2 the same, and shot 3 as a contre-jour halo 'from a big window behind the boy'. The scene only has the one window and a front door. Fix the light.
evals.expected_output: A repaired plan that notices shot 3 invents a source, and either declares the front door as a source switched on when it opens or relights the shot from the declared window.
assertions: The output identifies that 'a big window behind the boy' is a source the scene never declared.
The repair either declares the front door as a source with the event that switches it on, or relights shot 3 from the declared window with a stated key side.
The repaired shots still name a declared source and a key side relative to the lens.

evals.prompt: Plan a 10-second Seedance 2.5 sequence: in a dark stone library, a veiled elder commands a young man to cross the room and kneel. A literal walk would look like a zombie, so the audience should feel they lost the moment with him. The hall has wall sconces behind him and a cold window high on the left.
evals.expected_output: A plan with a push-in clip on his face, a declared light cue that switches the sconces off inside that shot, and a second clip that opens with him already kneeling, joined by a blink cut made in assembly. No clip shows the walk, and any defocus is left to post.
assertions: The sconces are declared with a position, and a cue on that source records a time, the change (off or dim), a trigger and the shot it lands in.
The push-in and the kneeling end state are separate clips generated at natural lengths, joined by an assembly blink cut rather than a cut requested inside one prompt.
No clip shows or prompts the walk across the room, and no prompt asks the model to skip it.
The plan does not prompt the face to drift out of focus; any defocus is assigned to post.
Every shot still names a declared source and a key side, and no shot invents a source that was not declared.

evals.prompt: A two-character interrogation: a seated elder dominates a kneeling young man for the first half, then he starts resisting and takes control. Plan the coverage so the power shift reads without dialogue explaining it.
evals.expected_output: A plan making the supplied resistance and control shift readable; a power-shift coverage pattern is one option, not a required shot recipe.
assertions: Shows the elder's initial dominance and the young man's resistance without inventing dialogue or a new outcome.
Any angle change or push-in supports the supplied shift; no specific move or framing is mandatory.
A held setup is valid if the physical exchange makes the shift readable.
May label the supplied turn without requiring exactly one turn shot.

evals.prompt: Plan the coverage for a 14-second Seedance 2.5 scene: a detective sees a bloodied glove in a locker and her two partners react behind her. Make the discovery land for the viewer.
evals.expected_output: A plan making the glove discovery and partners' reactions readable, with framing and featured subjects named; a look/POV/reaction sequence or held shared coverage can serve the brief.
assertions: The viewer can connect the detective's discovery to the glove; does not require a look/POV/reaction shot count.
Every shot names a framing and its featured subjects.
The partners' supplied reactions remain readable, in shared coverage or justified singles.
No minimum neighbor contrast or turn-shot quota substitutes for the discovery and response.

evals.prompt: A grandmother stands over her seated grandson at the dinner table and scolds him; halfway through he stands up and answers back. Cover it in four shots so the power shift reads from the camera alone.
evals.expected_output: A four-shot plan making the supplied standing/seated relationship and answer-back readable through camera choices; over-the-hip and a single are options, not mandatory coverage.
assertions: The initial standing/seated relationship remains readable without requiring a foreground mass or over-the-hip framing.
Once he stands, the camera coverage reflects the changed relationship without inventing a further action or outcome.
Every shot names a framing and featured subjects; the boy's response is readable without requiring a single.
Any change in foreground mass or angle serves the supplied power shift, without an exact change count.

evals.prompt: In my 6-second shot plan the camera pushes in on a woman's face, the focus slides off her face onto the wall behind her as she loses her grip, and at 4 s a half-second flash of her childhood bedroom cuts in. Plan it.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the push-in with ordinary focus, marks the defocus away from the face as a post treatment, and makes the half-second flash an assembly cut generated as its own clip.
assertions: The focus pull away from the face is not planned as prompt wording; it is marked for post, and the push-in keeps ordinary focus.
The half-second flash is planned as an assembly cut whose image is generated as its own clip at a natural length.
The plan names a light source and key side for the push-in and states its start and end.
The plan does not promise frame-accurate timing for the cut.

evals.prompt: Plan one 6-second two-shot: an adult frame-left hands a plain cup to an adult frame-right, featured=both, composition=balanced. No camera movement, grade or extra lighting requested.
evals.expected_output: A compact one-shot plan preserving the given sides, two featured adults, balanced composition and the cup handoff; unrequested axes are omitted.
assertions: The plan stays one 6-second two-shot with both adults featured and the supplied balanced composition.
Preserves frame-left giver and frame-right receiver and the plain cup handoff.
Does not invent a move, lens, grade or extra lighting to satisfy variety checks.
Does not split the handoff into multiple shots, save files or require a review gate.

evals.prompt: Plan a 12-second kitchen doorway surprise. The mother is inside; the aunt and boy are outside the closed door. The boy first appears after the mother opens it. Keep that appearance as the turn.
evals.expected_output: The establishing shot keeps the visitors hidden and the later shot retains the reveal.
expectations: The opening features only the mother; neither aunt nor boy appears through the closed door.
Framing and featured subjects preserve the first-appearance reveal.
Does not expose the hidden boy to meet a group-framing or count heuristic.

evals.prompt: Carry these locked shots into a framing plan: a low-angle over-the-shoulder shot from behind Mara, then an overhead first-person POV from her position. Do not change camera elevation.
evals.expected_output: Independent framing, viewpoint and physical angle retain both locks; variety scoring does not overwrite them.
expectations: The OTS retains angle low and its featured target.
The POV retains angle overhead and owner Mara.
Any derived comparison class counts once and does not replace angle or framing in the prompt.

evals.prompt: Plan coverage for three equal-length silent shots of an adult waiting for a kettle. All are held rear wide shots. The performance plan specifies sustained attention, no turn and no emotional change. Preserve the supplied framing, timing and light.
evals.expected_output: A chat-only plan preserving repeated stillness and equal timing without a forced turn, cut or motion quota.
expectations: Keeps all three held rear wide shots and equal lengths.
Carries sustained attention without revealing the face or inventing a tactic switch.
Does not add motion, contrast, a turn or light changes to satisfy V1-V10.
Does not create files, demand a scene manifest or run an automatic review.

evals.prompt: In chat, plan a locked 5-second medium two-shot. Beat b20: A picks up a bag and B tries to delay the departure with the exact Spanish line {No te vayas.}. A listens but leaves. No delivery recording or source file exists. Keep camera and light unchanged.
evals.expected_output: A provisional plan linking the supplied trigger, pursuit and listener response while keeping unresolved speech fit explicit.
expectations: Preserves beat b20, Spanish words, A's departure and the held two-shot.
Reserves space for the listener response and does not claim measured timing.
Accepts inline context without inventing source files, hashes or approved evidence.
Returns timing uncertainty without accelerating speech, rewriting dialogue or creating a review gate.

evals.prompt: Plan an energetic 10-second exchange. Two couriers hurry side by side; A says exactly {This way!} in English and darts left, B registers it and follows. Keep brisk footwork and a tracking medium two-shot, no fall, extra words or stop for speech. No delivery recording exists. Return in chat.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded energetic dialogue plan preserving the repeated steps, directional change and follower response without inserting speech holds.
expectations: Separates actor energy, camera tracking and edit rhythm; does not select restrained energy just because there is dialogue.
Preserves exact words, the left turn and B's registration, with weight transfer and recovery appropriate to brisk movement.
Keeps both subjects and the relevant response readable at the proposed framing and speed.
Leaves speech fit and actual motion unverified without playback; no automatic review, saved plan or generation.

evals.prompt: Plan a quiet 10-second counterpart: the same couriers wait side by side in a locked medium two-shot. A quietly says exactly {This way!} in English while looking toward the left doorway; B listens but deliberately waits. No steps, cut, turn of the body or added gesture. Return in chat.
evals.expected_output: A sustained quiet exchange preserving deliberate waiting and readable listening without borrowing urgency from the courier scenario.
expectations: Preserves the held medium two-shot, exact words and B's deliberate waiting.
Does not add movement, a reversal or a louder delivery to prove energy or aliveness.
Acceptance concerns readable orientation, exact delivery and sustained attention, not variety.
No files, automatic review or claim of observed media quality.
